_note: Structural layer first: pledge-works already produces its three registers in every sampled run, so semantic judges are built only where the code checks leave gaps. Two bars are deliberately not machine-checked: 'accepts outputs from any other skill in the set as pledge anchors' (no scenario in evals.json supplies another skill's output; food-delivery-pledges only describes audit findings in prose, so a check would test one scenario's wording, not the claim) and 'works at individual, team, and org-wide scope' (no scenario asks for a stated scope, and the three scenarios do not map to the three scopes). Add a scenario per scope or per upstream skill, then add the checks. Early-warning, consequence and cadence counts read the labelled lines the skill's Stage 3 template produces. The stress-test bar is checked by presence in code and, for the per-pledge claim, by a document-level semantic check because outputs legitimately stress-test pledges in groups ('P1/P4 at risk').

semantic.bar: every default-challenging pledge has an early warning indicator distinct from the failure signal
semantic.instructions: Is `items[{i}]` a leading indicator, an observable event or behavior that happens BEFORE the pledge is broken, rather than the breach or failure threshold itself?

criteria.true: Describes a precursor that can be observed while the pledge is still intact, such as a waiver request, a skipped review, a proposal to merge or remove a disclosure, or a metric drifting toward its threshold.
criteria.false: Restates the failure itself (the pledge has already been broken, or a number is already past its failure threshold), or is a vague worry with nothing observable.

semantic.bar: every default-challenging pledge has a stress test result and a named protective mechanism
semantic.instructions: In the pledge document `items[{i}]`, is every pledge marked default-challenging in the Pledge Register covered by a stress-test scenario that gives a result and names a protective mechanism (a process, approval gate or escalation path) for it? A mechanism written for a stated group of pledges covers each pledge in the group.

criteria.true: Every default-challenging pledge appears in a stress-test scenario, alone or as part of a named group, and each scenario names a concrete protective mechanism.
criteria.false: One or more default-challenging pledges have no stress test, or a scenario names only an intention ('leadership should hold firm') and no mechanism.

semantic.bar: every pledge has all five operationalization fields: quantitative success indicator (with number/threshold), quantitative failure signal (with breach threshold)
semantic.instructions: Could someone check `items[{i}]` against real data and say unambiguously whether it was met or breached?

criteria.true: States a measurable threshold -- a number or percentage ('95% of offers', '> 5% in a rolling week'), an absolute ('zero identifiable records leave'), or a specific event whose single occurrence counts ('any feature released without the checklist').
criteria.false: A direction or aspiration with no threshold, such as 'users feel more respected', 'improved accessibility over time', or 'fewer complaints'.
